text:
The Canucks are 4-17-1 with 9 points, and Sunday's 6-3 win in Vegas only ended a seven-game winless run. Our playoff simulations give them essentially no chance and project about 60 points. Under Manny Malhotra, this has become a season about what comes next.

That's why the headlines are about Elias Pettersson, the centre, and Jake DeBrusk. Reports say Carolina has renewed its pursuit of Pettersson and that a contender has checked in, while DeBrusk is drawing interest that Vancouver is said to be resisting at its current price. Brock Boeser, meanwhile, reached 500 career points and is on a seven-game point streak, which makes him the kind of player a rebuilding team has to think hard about.

The numbers are as bad as the record. Vancouver has 40.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 41% at five on five, and gives up 3.79 expected goals per 60. Both of Filip Hronek's pairings, with the young defenceman Elias Pettersson and with Zeev Buium, are around 35 to 37% of the chances. And the goaltending has made it worse: 14 goals beyond expected allowed, with Kevin Lankinen at .802 and 0-5 over his last five starts. Our model rates the Canucks almost seven points unluckier than their play, which says how far the floor has fallen.

Watch the trade market, Buium's minutes and whether Leevi Merilainen gets more of the net.
